name: snoopy-88f23fce-blind30
instr:
# Diagnosing a2o/snoopy without a test suite

Software here is supposed to write a record of every command any program on the machine executes, by way of code loaded ahead of everything else, and a small command line tool ships alongside it for switching that recording on and for showing how it is set up. Both that tool and the records now come out wrong in a great many ways. Nothing about the machine or the programs being watched changed. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Reaching for the small tool at a shell. Every operation asked of it aborts at once, protesting that the shared object it depends on cannot be read, so even asking which version the tool is, or which version that shared object is, produces an error rather than a number. Asking it to print the settings in force yields unpopulated or default values instead of them, and that same request also shows built-in defaults where the values supplied by the settings file belong. Asking for its about text or its help text prints nothing at all, and a keyword it does not recognise neither prints usage nor exits with a failure code. Asking it to switch recording on writes its own entry into the file naming what is loaded ahead of everything else with the final character cut off. Asking it to report what is currently set up misdescribes that same file's contents, giving the wrong text when such an entry is present, when it is duplicated, and when it belongs to something else.
